subject: DPA: EU residency & deletion language — follow-up and proposed compromises
messages:
From: Anne Keller <anne.keller@aurumhealth.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: Sage Contracts <contracts@aurumhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2029 08:14:00 +0200
Subject: DPA redline — questions on deletion scope and onshore backups

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for sending the latest DPA redline (attached). We're reviewing and the legal team has three points that need clarification before we can move to commercial approval:

1) Deletion request timing: Section 4.2 says "Redwood will delete customer data on request within a commercially reasonable time." Our counsel needs specific windows (we proposed 30 days). Can you confirm the fastest commitment you can make for EU production data (not including logs/backups)?

2) Backups & restoration copies: The draft keeps backups in scope but is vague about restore/retention for backup media. If a data subject request is made, will backups be purged/overwritten within a defined window? We need a commitment or a clear carveout.

3) Residency guarantees: The redline allows "logical processing" in non-EU zones for redundancy. For our pilot customers handling PHI-like data, we need a Geo-lock guarantee or an explicit fallback plan and evidence we can use during audit.

Attached: Redline_DPA_v2.docx and a high-level data flow map. Can we get proposed language and an evidence timeline (how long to produce a deletion certificate)?

Appreciate a quick turnaround — our procurement deadline is 24 May.

Best,
Anne
Anne Keller
Head of Procurement
Aurum Health

---
Attachments: Redline_DPA_v2.docx (docx), data_flow_map_v3.pdf (pdf)

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Anne Keller <anne.keller@aurumhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 17 May 2029 11:02:00 +0200
Subject: Re: DPA redline — questions on deletion scope and onshore backups

Hi Anne — thanks for the clear note and the deadline. I've looped in Marissa (Legal) and Ben (Account) to help with specifics. High level answers while legal drafts formal redline text: 

- Deletion timing: operational data deletion can be initiated immediately upon a verified erasure request. We can propose two commitments: acknowledgement+initiation within 48 hours, and full logical deletion of customer data (excluding backups) within 30 days.

- Backups: We treat backups as separate retention buckets. For backups we can commit to not using backups for restore after a deletion request and to an overwrite policy that removes affected customer blocks within 180 days; we can provide a certificate of overwrite within 30 days after the overwrite completes.

- Residency: For your EU pilot we can offer zone-locking for primary processing and storage. Fallback to non-EU zones would be an opt-in carveout and only used under explicit failover conditions; any such behavior would be auditable and recorded in logs we can share.

This is our starting position — Marissa will suggest precise contract language and a short set of carveouts for lawful holds and disaster recovery. If that aligns, Ben and I can propose a DocuSign-ready redline and a short Audit Evidence SLA. Can we do a 30-minute call Monday to finalize?

Thanks,
Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Sales, EMEA
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Anne Keller <anne.keller@aurumhealth.com>, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 17 May 2029 15:40:00 +0200
Subject: RE: DPA redline — proposed contract language (draft)

Stephanie/Anne — drafting notes below; I'm attaching a marked-up redline with bracketed compromise language. High-level legal position: we want to be precise about timelines while preserving legitimate DR/forensic exceptions. Suggested contract language (proposed edits to Section 4.2 and 4.3):

- "Erasure request and initiation: Upon Customer's verified request, Redwood will acknowledge receipt within forty-eight (48) hours and will initiate erasure processes for Customer Data within seventy-two (72) hours."

- "Completion windows: Excluding data in immutable backups, Redwood will complete logical deletion of Customer Data in production and operational copies within thirty (30) calendar days of initiation. For data contained in backups, Redwood will (i) discontinue restore from affected backup media immediately upon initiation, and (ii) overwrite or deallocate the affected backup blocks in accordance with Redwood's backup lifecycle, which will not exceed one hundred eighty (180) calendar days from initiation, except where retention is required by law or a litigation hold."

- "Certification and evidence: Upon Customer request, Redwood will provide a written certificate of deletion within thirty (30) calendar days after the deletion (or overwrite) action completes. For the avoidance of doubt, metadata and aggregated telemetry that are not Customer Data as defined in the DPA are excluded from these erasure commitments."

- "Residency/service geography: For Customers electing the 'EU Zone Lock' option (as described in Appendix A), primary storage and processing will occur in EU-located regions. Redwood will not route persistent customer content to non-EU regions except for (a) temporary, in-flight processing for latency-sensitive routing, or (b) explicit, agreed failover events. Any cross-border processing will be logged and reported in the Audit Evidence SLA."

I added bracketed text for the "failover events" definition — please see the attached redline for exact phrasing. 

Open items for negotiation: (1) whether overwrite window can be shortened to 90 days for pilot customers, (2) whether we need monthly deletion certification or upon-request only, and (3) whether the EU Zone Lock can be a contract-level guarantee vs an "option" on Dedicated capacity.

Anne — happy to jump on Monday with Stephanie and Ben. If you can share the procurement team's acceptable windows around backups (90 vs 180) and certification frequency (on-request vs monthly), we can close this fast.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Data Protection
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: Redline_DPA_v2_marked.docx (docx), audit_evidence_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Anne Keller <anne.keller@aurumhealth.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Sage Contracts <contracts@aurumhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2029 09:12:00 +0200
Subject: Re: DPA redline — backup window and certification questions

Thanks Marissa — useful draft. A few clarifications from our side before the call: 

- Overwrite window: Our legal team will accept 180 days for standard customers, but for the EU pilot (Aurum Pilot Wave 1) we require a 90-day max for backups. The pilot contains sensitive PII/PHI analogs and we want a stricter window for that cohort.

- Certification cadence: we prefer on-request certificates for cost reasons, but we require Redwood to commit to producing certificates within thirty (30) days of request, and to provide quarterly deletion roll-up reports during the pilot.

- Zone lock: we appreciate the 'option' approach. For procurement, we need the Zone Lock available as a contract-level option for customers in the pilot — i.e., selectable at contract signature without an architecture change. If that is a technical gating issue, confirm what operational steps and timeline are required to enable it.

If those three items can be captured in the redline, I think we can hit procurement's 24 May deadline. We'll be on the call Monday at 10:00 CEST.

Best,
Anne

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Anne Keller <anne.keller@aurumhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 21 May 2029 17:03:00 +0200
Subject: Re: DPA redline — alignment and next steps

Anne — thanks for the clear priorities. Quick summary of agreed compromises and next actions so we have a single source of truth before Monday's call: 

1) Backups overwrite window: Redwood accepts 90 days for the specific "Aurum Pilot Wave 1" cohort; default customers remain at 180 days. We'll mark this as a pilot-level schedule in Appendix B.

2) Certification & reporting: Certificates of deletion will be provided on-request within 30 days of request. During the pilot Redwood will additionally produce a quarterly deletion roll-up report and make that available in the Console's audit export.

3) Zone Lock: Technical team confirms EU Zone Lock can be selected at contract signature for Dedicated or Hosted accounts where region capacity is available; activation timeline is typically 3-7 business days from signature for Hosted and up to 10 business days for Dedicated provisioning. We will include a statement in Appendix A referencing those timelines and an opt-in flag in the order form.

Next steps: Marissa will incorporate the above into the redline and produce a DocuSign-ready DPA by EOD Monday. Ben will follow up offline on pilot pricing and order-form language. Anne — if that timeline works, we'll circulate the updated redline and a DocuSign link and schedule a short 15-minute alignment call post-signature to confirm activation steps.

Thanks all — appreciate the collaborative tone here.

Steph
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Sales, EMEA
Redwood Inference
